name: Maldives
rule: The Attorney General’s current consolidated Plant Protection Act 12/2011, section 36, defines plants as living plants/parts (including seeds) and distinguishes unchanged/unmanufactured plant material, including grain, from manufactured products whose manner of manufacture leaves a risk of introducing or spreading pests. Sections 19 and 22 require certificates and permits for those defined controlled goods. Section 20(b) ties phytosanitary measures to applicable international standards or technical justification. Applied to the specified factory-made sencha (steamed, repeatedly rolled/pressed with hot air, dried and finished), these domestic category boundaries support a no-special-phytosanitary-document conclusion: it is a manufactured food, not living or merely raw dried plant material, and ISPM 32 section 2 Category 1 / Appendix 2 expressly identifies tea as an example of manufacture that removes plant-pest risk. This is a reasoned application of Maldivian statutory scope, not a claim that ISPM membership itself creates a waiver. The December 2025 and March 2026 ministry instructions govern covered plants/products and do not expressly expand section 36 to all finished food. Separately, MFDA-FCD STAN6-2021 Rev.1 November 2025 permits personal processed food up to 5 kg/5 litres with intact identifiable packaging; its special advance postal form is for breast-milk substitutes, not tea. Section 37 of the 2011 Act expressly repeals Plant Quarantine Regulation 2008, so its old packed-food language is not relied upon as current authority.
personalMailApplicability: General commodity-scope interpretation applies equally to postal imports. Act section 25(b) expressly names post and courier services when handling covered plants/products/regulated articles; it does not make an otherwise outside-scope finished food a controlled commodity. This conclusion does not borrow a passenger allowance. The separate current MFDA standard governs the recipient’s noncommercial food use, including small parcels.

quantityLimit.text: MFDA-FCD STAN6-2021 Rev.1 November 2025, section 4.1, printed page 4: personal processed foods must not exceed 5 kg NET WEIGHT (5 litres for liquids). The dry tea limit uses net grams.
quantityLimit.scope: Processed-food category collectively; allowance is not stated per tea variety. Category-wide aggregation in one consignment is the conservative application; the text does not explicitly define a parcel/time interval.

authority: Maldives Ministry of Agriculture and Animal Welfare, Plant Protection Section; Ministry of Health
researchAttempts: Read the current December 2025 phytosanitary importer notice.
Checked the agriculture ministry downloads and searched for tea/processed-food classifications.
Located the personal-food import standard but did not treat food quantities as a phytosanitary waiver.
Located the current revised noncommercial-food standard, published 7 January 2026, but official PDF requests returned HTTP 403; did not rely on the older personal-food download as current.

Checked the ministry mandate (Plant Protection Act 2011/12), current notices and commodity searches. Coconut-palm/nursery permit instructions are not evidence for manufactured tea. No applicable tea exemption located.

Retried the revised MFDA PDF through web research: all 8 pages became readable despite direct HTTP still returning 403. Read sections 1, 4, 6.2 and 9: processed-food limit 5 kg/5 litres, packaging/identity and personal-use evidence; the advance postal clearance in 6.2 is specific to breast-milk substitutes and was not misapplied to tea.

30 September independent food-rule closure check: the existing review already read current MFDA-FCD STAN6-2021 Rev.1 November 2025 (published January 2026), including its processed-food 5 kg/5 litre personal allowance and the breast-milk-substitute-specific postal form. New attempts to reopen the current Ministry publication/PDF returned inaccessible tool responses and supplied no contrary rule. Did not apply commercial food licensing or the breast-milk-substitute clearance form to ordinary tea. Retained the prior current-standard findings and the separate unresolved agricultural classification.

30 September bounded remaining-scope review: Located the NPPO-filed 2011 Plant Protection Act uploaded to IPPC on 12 June 2025. Web-indexed Dhivehi text was readable; direct PDF download returned 403 and screenshot retrieval failed. A provisional reading of articles 19–22 and the definitions does not establish a finished-tea exemption; it is not an official English translation. The older English Plant Quarantine Regulation distinguishes planting material from dried/packed food, but cannot independently settle the later Act and current notice. WTO 2024 paragraph 3.101 identifies Agriculture Online System as a requirements source; its public URL redirects to a login and exposes no commodity conditions. No sign-in or account creation attempted.

30 September fresh official-source recovery: government law-index embedded data exposed current consolidation 201/238 and original PDF. Recovered the complete HTML/structured text with an ordinary User-Agent request, generated PDF, and original PDF via its normal download query. The original Dhivehi Act was read with unofficial English paraphrases, and the relevant original definition page visually checked. Section 36 risk-qualified manufacture, section 20(b) international-standard/technical-justification basis, section 25 express postal handling and section 37 repeal are now fully available. No new contrary specific tea condition was located. The IPPC global index separately lists a Plant Protection Regulation uploaded June 2025, but its report page returns a navigation shell without the report/attachment; this unavailable listing is not treated as an operative contrary rule or affirmative exemption.

Re-read and downloaded original current MFDA8-page standard. Printed p4§4.1 expressly uses net weight and not exceeding5kg/5L; category-wide aggregate wording does not define a per-parcel/time interval or confer a per-variety allowance. Sections1.10 and1.11 concern recipient identity and limited whole-unit rounding; no numerical uplift used. Added quantityLimitKg5 with precise legal-net versus conservative-store-gross distinction.

30 September original current eight-page MFDA PDF recovered and section 4.1 visually checked: explicit inclusive 5 kg NET WEIGHT. Corrected the report to 5000 net grams and 50 exact 100 g pouches; the earlier suggested 41 gross-weight bag sizing is not the legal food limit. The provision does not grant 5 kg separately for each tea variety; category-wide consignment aggregation is expressly labelled an interpretation.
permitFreeReason: Supported by the domestic section 36 living/unmanufactured/risk-qualified manufactured-product boundary applied to fully manufactured sencha, with ISPM 32 tea Category 1 as technical evidence and the current MFDA personal-food allowance. This is an interpretive conclusion from published general law, not an express Maldives tea-specific ruling or a personal exemption from controls on raw plant material.
requiredDocument: Ordinary postal/customs declaration and any routine arrival food inspection; no separate plant permit or phytosanitary certificate under the stated general-category interpretation.
foodImportReview: Current MFDA personal-food conditions verified: 5 kg/5 litres of processed food, intact identifiable packaging, and personal-use evidence if requested; the advance postal breast-milk-substitute form does not apply to tea.
finding: Recovered complete current Attorney General consolidation, all statutory sections and the original 25-page PDF. Confirmed section 36 definitions, sections 19–22 import controls, section 25 postal handling and section 37 express repeal of the 2008 regulation. Original printed page 24 was visually checked against the structured official text.
interpretationCaveat: Source law is official Dhivehi; English descriptions are the reviewer’s paraphrase, not an official translation. Supported is conditional on the recorded manufacture, pure tea content, clean sealed retail packing, absence of soil/seeds/raw untreated additions or raw-wood packing, and genuinely private consumption. Ordinary inspection and enforcement against contaminated goods remain available. Sections 19/22 would require unavailable special documents if the product instead met the controlled definitions. No claim of a regulator-specific advance tea approval is made.
quantityLimitBasis: Explicit net-weight threshold in original Dhivehi section 4.1, independently read and visually checked. Fifty 100 g pouches = 5 kg net. Packaging is not included in this MFDA net limit. Other processed foods share the category allowance under the stated aggregate interpretation.

quantitySourceReview.aggregation: Processed-food category; no per-product or per-variety allowance stated. Section4.1 does not expressly define parcel/time interval. Category-wide aggregation for the consignment is conservative application.

otherProvisions.1.10: Personal food imported in intended person’s name; company-name imports treated as commercial.
otherProvisions.1.11: Limited rounding to a whole product unit where meeting the standard quantity requires at least half that final unit. No uplift used in store policy.
otherProvisions.2.1: Fruit/vegetable category separately and expressly total together on one occasion; do not silently copy its exact words into4.1.
otherProvisions.4.2: Package must not be damaged/leaking and label must identify food.

quantitySourceReview.translation: Reviewer paraphrase of official Dhivehi; net-weight loanword is explicit.
